utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, our submission is that you are in a position to verify it. It's a video that's on the Prosecution's 65 ter list. And we would suggest that since there is evidence that the witness has fabricated his evidence, we actually tender this for admission. Its 65 ter 2608 to 2610.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we were not able, but you're now enabling us to verify. Could you -- I do not know whether the footage you're talking about is the same footage as Mr. Bakrac was talking about, because, of course, in the statement, we can't see which 65 ter number -- or is it on your list --

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The witness -- oh, yes. The statement only -- the statement refers to footage on TV --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: -- of the Serbian MUP, and Mr. Bakrac picked up on it and asked whether he was fabricating due to Serbian TV footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The witness, in his answer, said "The Unit Jedenica," which is the name of the footage. It's clear, I think, that they're talking about same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... response to your question, or is it just -- let me --

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes in response to my following up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So what I would like to do is to invite the parties to agree on whether that is the footage the witness was referring to. We have now his answer. And then we are able to look at it if we want to, but, again, this is a matter which has not -- I mean, if you start exploring a matter which has some importance, then finish that exploration rather than stop it halfway and leave the Chamber with question marks rather than any assistance. That's my point, as a matter of fact. Now everyone is -- I would -- I have no problems in -- I take it, but I should consult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber is quite willing look at the footage which is suggested to be the source of inspiration for the witness. And then at least we know what we are talking about. Until now, we had no clue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm sorry to leap up again. It's not strictly my issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But I'm afraid the witness didn't say the film was called "The Unit." He said the footage showed the unit itself. So we really aren't in agreement that this is the footage -- the footage is the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's ask the witness. You said you had seen a television footage. Do you remember the title of that footage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I, as a witness, must clarify something here. It's something that was shown on TV. It was seen by the general public. But what I'm saying is not based on what was shown on TV. I'm testifying about the time period when I was in the disco, detained there. So I'm not basing my testimony on this footage that was shown on TV and could be seen by anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your testimony in this respect is perfectly clear. Let's let there be no doubt about that, that you say, "I didn't testify on the basis of what I saw on television, but I testified on the basis of what I saw at the time when I was detained there." Nevertheless, my question: Do you remember the title of the footage you are referring to that you saw on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It had to do with Serbia and problems in Serbia related to the assassination of Djindjic. So it was not really related to the events that I'm now testifying about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't remember the title?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was called "The Unit." That was the name of the programme.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was called "The Unit," that being clarified. Now, as I said before, the Chamber is -- if there's any -- Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have the video. We're uploading it now, if it would assist, just the opening, to see if the witness could confirm if that's what he saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if the title is known, if the circumstances under which it -- unless there are two or three items under the name "The Unit" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I merely quoted from his statement that he saw video footage about the Serbian MUP. I don't see any reason why this should be dealt with in examination-in-chief. And we oppose this line of questioning. And I merely wanted to see if any footage that he saw on TV might have influenced his views. And it is not proper to conduct the examination-in-chief in the course of the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber considers the matter to be dealt with. If there's any need for a follow-up, the Chamber will further invite the parties to make further submissions. Was that your last question, Ms. Friedman?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Just one point of clarification, Your Honour. We did tender the exhibit. Is there a ruling on whether it's admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- you mean in the -- you tendered it?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: We're tendering it on the basis that there has been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but when did you tender it?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... an allegation of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes. On basis of the allegation of fabrication, we asked to have it admitted, and I wanted to know if there was a ruling on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There is no ruling on it yet. We'll consider that matter. We don't have to ask the witness unless you consider it really necessary to -- the only thing the witness said is, "I saw similar --" that's the only thing he says. Patches -- I have seen footage on the Red Berets where I have seen the same insignia as I had seen in the Doboj area. That's all he says. Nothing more, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: He, though, was asked -- he was told that his whole testimony is based on the film footage, so that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: So that was the point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Asked by apparently Mr. Bakrac not having seen or not having inquired into what the video footage would have been, just on the basis of this, that you suggested this to the witness, Mr. Bakrac. Is that -- you did it purely and exclusively on the basis of what you read in paragraph 29. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's why I don't think that -- examination-in-chief should not be conducted in the course of the re-examination. And, secondly, what can this witness tell us about it? The footage exists. It is in front of you. You can disrule on it. The witness cannot tell us anything more about this footage that would assist you in your decision whether to admit it or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what was suggested is that he would identify the footage as the one he had seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will decide on the matter. Of course, we're not going to admit into evidence anything which we have not seen yet, so therefore there will be an opportunity to further deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to raise the matter on short -- in the short term. Any further questions? Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Since we are now hopelessly delayed and we cannot start addressing the administrative issues, the housekeeping matters, let me just follow up on what my learned friend Ms. Friedman asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, you explained what the distance was between the place where you were and the doorway of Percin's Disco. On the 12th, in the morning, you say that there was gunfire coming from all directions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that once there was gunfire, the gunfire was heard, everybody stood up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some people stood up. Some remained sitting down. We were simply afraid because the gunfire was getting closer and closer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the 15 metres there were at least 50 people -- people who were taken out immediately after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS JF-008 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to clarify one thing with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No, please, do not clarify anything with me. I'm asking you: Is it true that there were at least 50 people in front of you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, if the witness starts his answer by saying, "I have to clarify one thing with you," then he's beginning to answer the question, you should not stop him and say him -- tell him that he should not clarify anything, because that is, apparently, part of his answer. The question that was put to you that in the room you were in, that 50 people were taken out of that, and Mr. Bakrac then referred to the size of the room at least the distance between you and the door. Could you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Let me respond. So when you get into the disco itself, the doorway, as soon as you get in, there is a very wide area to the left and to the right. So that's the width of the room. That's the greatest size. So there was a huge number of people to the left and to the right and in front of the doorway itself. And I was about 15 metres away from the doorway, and so I was able to see the people who got in. And I could see the 50 people who were taken out, but they were both in front of me and to the left and to the right. That's what I wanted to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. This, then, concludes your tell, Witness JF-008. I'd like to thank you very much for coming a long way to The Hague and for having answered all the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Judges. And I would like to -- you don't receive interpretation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- I started saying that this concludes your testimony, that we would like to thank you very much for coming the long way to The Hague, and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench. And we wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind to follow the Usher who will escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I leave it to the parties whether they would like to use the remaining eight minutes to start with the housekeeping session or whether we would see each other again tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We have no strong views on it Your Honour, whichever pleases --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No strong views.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No strong views.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's get started.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since I examined the witness, the housekeeping matters will be addressed by my colleague Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's get started. The first one is the joint submission of maps. An agreement exists between the parties on the 22 maps from the map binder. First of all, I would like to clarify which maps we are talking about. In the binder, the maps on which the parties agree that they jointly seek them to be admitted into evidence are the numbers 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 19, 20, 21, 23, 24, 29, 32, 33, 35, 37, and 38. Those maps are to be uploaded under one exhibit number, all of them together. And I already asked Madam Registrar to assign a number to this -- that series of maps which will be uploaded by the Office of the Prosecution but on joint request. Madam Registrar, could you already assign a number to the series of maps.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P258, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P258, since not yet uploaded, still be marked for identification at this moment, although it's a bit silly to mark something for identification if you've not seen it. But to be uploaded and, once uploaded, to inform the Chamber so that we can change the status from MFI into admitted into evidence. To avoid whatever misunderstanding, other maps of which I did not read out the numbers may already have been admitted into evidence. Some of the maps from the binder are already in evidence and are not included in this P258 number. The Chamber, and I'm now moving to my next subject, the Chamber will give a ruling on the Prosecution's motion for admission of redacted copies of confidential exhibits as public exhibits in due course, but already instructs the Prosecution to prepare and read out short summaries of the written evidence admitted for each witness to inform the public. This should obviously not be done for witnesses with closed session protective measures. Further, the OTP is instructed to file public summaries of past witnesses, that is, C-015, Savic Denona [sic] -- no. I'm misreading. Witness Savic, Witness Denona, Witness Kirudja, Witness Kovacevic, Witness Hadzovic, Witness Miljanic, Witness JF-006, Witness JF-007, Witness JF-005, Witness Tihic, Witness Lazarevic, Witness JF-009. Those are the witnesses. The reasons for all this, enabling the public to follow these proceedings, especially for 92 witnesses are about. I add to the list Witness JF-008 who testified today, of course, to the extent that his testimony was public which was not all of his testimony. It's 7.00. We will adjourn for the day, and I announce with some regret that we adjourn until -- until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Petrovic. I wanted to finish my line by saying until the 19th of -- the 19th of February at 9.00 in the morning. But before I finally do so --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I only wanted to ask you. I don't know what the procedure is and whether it is necessary to put that on the record. I just wanted to ask you on behalf of my client, Mr. Simatovic, to relieve him of his duty to be here. He doesn't want to be here tomorrow, so I don't know whether -- what's the custom, whether I should really announce it so that it is put on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wanted to, as a matter of fact, ask the witnesses -- ask the accused whether they wanted to be present or not. I think early already it was this -- Friday morning was arranged for Mr. Stanisic not being present that morning hours that third day in the week. I now see that Mr. Simatovic would prefer not to be present as well. You're both excused. It's the fate of lawyers that they have to attend these meetings. Therefore, it's fully accepted that you'd rather stay out, although it's still part of your case, let there be no doubt about it. And decisions to be announced and matters to be raised are not without substance and not without relevance. But the Chamber accepts your choice. Therefore, we --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it appears that they do not understand -- they do understand that it's important for their case, but they trust their lawyers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's -- trust is a good thing. We adjourn, and we resume tomorrow, 19th of February, 9.00 in the morning in this same courtroom, Courtroom II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of February, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
